question:
Fill in the blank with the correct idiom selecting from the given alternatives.

Though he had contributed almost nothing to the project, he demanded the ______ of the profits.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. lion's share.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "the lion's share" means the largest or the best part of something, especially a part that is out of all proportion to what one deserves. (सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा)
◦ Example: The lion's share of the budget was spent on infrastructure.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *Though he had contributed almost nothing to the project, he demanded the lion's share of the profits.* The sense of an unfair and disproportionate claim fits the idiom exactly.

 

• The expression comes from Aesop's fable, in which the lion, having hunted with other animals, claims every portion of the kill for himself on one pretext or another.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The remaining alternatives — "tiger's share", "wolf's share" and "fox's share" — are not established English idioms at all. Each has been formed by simply replacing "lion" with the name of another animal, and none of them carries any accepted meaning in English.

 

NOTE

 

• Other animal idioms frequently asked in SSC: "A dog in the manger" (one who prevents others from enjoying what he cannot use), "To let the cat out of the bag" (to reveal a secret), "A wolf in sheep's clothing" (a dangerous person pretending to be harmless), "To take the bull by the horns" (to face a difficulty boldly) and "A white elephant" (a costly but useless possession).

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

A baker's dozen.
option_1: A very small and inadequate quantity
option_2: A bargain that favours only one party
option_3: A payment made in kind instead of cash
option_4: A group or quantity of thirteen
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A group or quantity of thirteen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "a baker's dozen" means thirteen, that is, one more than the usual dozen of twelve. (तेरह की संख्या)
◦ Example: She came back from the market with a baker's dozen of eggs.

 

• The origin lies in medieval England, where bakers who sold underweight bread faced severe penalties. To be safe, a baker would add one extra loaf to every batch of twelve, and the practice gave the language its name for thirteen.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 describes idioms such as "a drop in the ocean" or "a mere trifle".

 

• Option 2 describes "a one-sided bargain" or the idiom "to have the lion's share".

 

• Option 3 describes "payment in kind", which is a plain expression and not an idiom at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Other number-based idioms often tested: "At sixes and sevens" (in a state of confusion), "To be in seventh heaven" (extremely happy), "A nine days' wonder" (something that attracts attention only briefly), "To talk nineteen to the dozen" (to talk very fast) and "The eleventh hour" (the last possible moment).

question: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Accommodation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Accommodation" — a room, building or space in which somebody may live or stay. (आवास / निवास स्थान)
◦ Example: The department provided free accommodation to the newly appointed staff.

 

• Spelling key: double "c" and double "m" — AC-COM-MO-DA-TION. A useful memory aid is that the word is large enough to *accommodate* two c's and two m's.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Accomodation" — incorrect; only one "m" has been used. This is by far the commonest error with this word.

 

• Option 2: "Acommodation" — incorrect; only one "c" has been used.

 

• Option 4: "Accomadation" — incorrect; "a" has been written in place of the second "o".

 

NOTE

 

• The verb is accommodate and the adjective accommodating (obliging, willing to help).

 

• Other double-letter words frequently misspelt: Committee, Occurrence, Embarrass, Harass, Millennium, Possession, Necessary (one c, two s) and Recommend (one c, two m).

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option 4 "No replacement required".

The regiment was admired for the camaraderee that existed among its officers and men.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. camaraderie.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word in the sentence, "camaraderee", is misspelt. The correct spelling is "camaraderie", ending in "-erie". (सौहार्द / भाईचारा)

 

• "Camaraderie" means mutual trust, warmth and friendship among people who spend a great deal of time together, especially companions in work or in arms.
◦ Example: The camaraderie among the members of the team was evident throughout the tournament.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The regiment was admired for the camaraderie that existed among its officers and men.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "cameraderie" — incorrect; an extra "e" has been inserted after "cam", making it look like "camera".

 

• Option 3: "camraderie" — incorrect; the "a" after "cam" has been dropped.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because the given word is misspelt and therefore does require replacement.

 

NOTE

 

• The word is borrowed from French, from *camarade*, meaning comrade.

 

• Other French-derived words with difficult endings: reverie, menagerie, lingerie, patisserie, connoisseur, entrepreneur and rendezvous.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The manager's arrogent behaviour towards his colleagues eventually damaged the reputation of the entire department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. arrogent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "arrogent". The correct spelling is "arrogant", ending in "-ant", not "-ent". (अहंकारी / घमंडी)

 

• "Arrogant" means having or showing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance, and behaving in an overbearing manner towards others.
◦ Example: His arrogant manner made him unpopular with the junior staff.

 

• The corrected sentence reads: *The manager's arrogant behaviour towards his colleagues eventually damaged the reputation of the entire department.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "colleagues" — correctly spelt; note the "ea" in the middle and the ending "-gue".

 

• Option 3: "eventually" — correctly spelt; note the double "l" before "-y".

 

• Option 4: "reputation" — correctly spelt.

 

NOTE

 

• Words ending in "-ant": *arrogant, relevant, brilliant, tolerant, significant, defiant, elegant, ignorant.*

 

• Words ending in "-ent": *different, excellent, independent, persistent, competent, apparent, consistent.*

 

• The noun form here is arrogance; note that adjectives in "-ant" usually take "-ance", and those in "-ent" take "-ence".

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Concesion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Concesion". The correct spelling is "Concession", with a double "s". (रियायत / छूट)

 

• "Concession" means something granted or yielded, especially a reduction in price or a point conceded in an argument.
◦ Example: Senior citizens are entitled to a concession in railway fares.

 

• The word comes from the verb "concede", and the "-de" ending changes to "-ssion" in the noun — just as *possess* gives *possession* and *express* gives *expression*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Possession" — correctly spelt; note the two pairs of double "s".

 

• Option 2: "Profession" — correctly spelt.

 

• Option 3: "Progression" — correctly spelt.

 

NOTE

 

• Rule of thumb for -sion and -tion:
◦ Verbs ending in -de, -d or -se usually take -sion: *decide → decision, conclude → conclusion, expand → expansion, concede → concession.*
◦ Verbs ending in -t or -te usually take -tion: *act → action, educate → education, relate → relation.*

 

• Frequently confused pairs in SSC: suspension (not "suspention"), extension (not "extention"), attention, intention and retention.

question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "condemn".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Applaud.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Condemn" means to express complete disapproval of something; to censure or denounce strongly. (निंदा करना)
◦ Example: The council condemned the attack on the relief workers.

 

• "Applaud" means to express approval or praise, and is therefore the correct antonym. (सराहना करना)
◦ Example: The audience applauded the young musician's performance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Denounce (भर्त्सना करना): To condemn publicly — a synonym of condemn, not an antonym.

 

• Option 2: Criticise (आलोचना करना): To point out faults — again close in sense to condemn.

 

• Option 4: Reproach (उलाहना देना): To express disapproval or disappointment to someone — a synonym rather than an opposite.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of condemn: Censure, Reprove, Rebuke, Castigate, Deplore, Decry.

 

• Synonyms of applaud: Commend, Extol, Laud, Acclaim, Eulogise, Compliment.

 

• Note the second sense of condemn — to sentence someone to a punishment, as in *condemned to life imprisonment*, and to declare a building unfit for use.

question: Choose the word that is the antonym of "Prosperity".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Adversity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Prosperity" means a state of flourishing, thriving and being successful, especially in financial terms. (समृद्धि / खुशहाली)
◦ Example: The new irrigation project brought prosperity to the region.

 

• "Adversity" means a state of hardship, misfortune or difficulty, and is therefore the correct antonym. (विपत्ति / संकट)
◦ Example: He bore his adversity with remarkable patience.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Affluence (सम्पन्नता): The state of having a great deal of money — a synonym of prosperity.

 

• Option 2: Opulence (वैभव): Great wealth and luxuriousness — again a synonym.

 

• Option 4: Abundance (प्रचुरता): A very large quantity of something — close in sense to prosperity rather than opposite to it.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of prosperity: Wealth, Success, Well-being, Plenty, Boom.

 

• Synonyms of adversity: Hardship, Misfortune, Distress, Tribulation, Affliction, Calamity.

 

• A well-known proverb worth remembering: "A friend in need is a friend indeed", and "Adversity is the true test of friendship."

question:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.

The office placed a bulk order for ______ before the beginning of the new session.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. stationery.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Stationery" is a noun meaning writing materials such as paper, pens, envelopes and files. (लेखन सामग्री) It is the word required here, since the office is ordering supplies.
◦ Example: The clerk was asked to check the stock of stationery in the store.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The office placed a bulk order for stationery before the beginning of the new session.*

 

• A reliable memory aid: stationEry contains "e" as in envelope, while stationAry contains "a" as in at rest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "stationary" (स्थिर): An adjective meaning not moving, fixed in one place — *The train remained stationary for twenty minutes.*

 

• Option 2: "stationer" (लेखन सामग्री विक्रेता): A person or shop that sells stationery. One buys stationery *from* a stationer, so the word does not fit the blank.

 

• Option 3: "statuary" (मूर्तिकला): Statues considered collectively, or the art of making them — unrelated in meaning.

 

NOTE

 

• Other frequently tested confusable pairs: principal/principle, complement/compliment, council/counsel, canvas/canvass, dessert/desert, personal/personnel and eminent/imminent.

question:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.

The medicine had a remarkable ______ on the patient within a few hours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. effect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Effect" is chiefly a noun meaning a result or an outcome. Since the blank follows the article "a" and the adjective "remarkable", a noun is required here. (प्रभाव / परिणाम)
◦ Example: The new policy had a positive effect on rural employment.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The medicine had a remarkable effect on the patient within a few hours.*

 

• The standard rule: "affect" is normally the verb and "effect" the noun. A useful mnemonic is RAVEN — Remember, Affect is a Verb, Effect is a Noun.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "affect" (प्रभावित करना): A verb meaning to influence or to produce a change in — *The drought affected the standing crop.* It cannot follow "a remarkable".

 

• Option 2: "afflict" (पीड़ित करना): A verb meaning to cause pain or suffering to somebody — *He was afflicted with arthritis.* Wrong in both form and sense.

 

• Option 4: "effuse": A rare verb meaning to pour out or give off; it is not used as a noun and does not fit the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• Note the exceptions: "effect" can be a verb meaning to bring about — *The committee effected several changes*; and "affect" can be a noun in psychology, meaning observed emotion.

 

• Related noun: "effective" (producing the intended result) and "efficient" (working without waste of effort or resources).

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The new officer is well versed ______ the rules of departmental procedure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "well versed in", meaning thoroughly familiar with, or highly skilled and knowledgeable in a subject. (निपुण / पारंगत)
◦ Example: She is well versed in the provisions of the Right to Information Act.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The new officer is well versed in the rules of departmental procedure.*

 

• The preposition "in" is regularly used with words expressing proficiency or expertise in a field — *skilled in, proficient in, experienced in, expert in, deficient in.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "at" is used with "good at, bad at, clever at, quick at" — *He is good at mathematics* — but not with "versed".

 

• Option 3: "with" is used with "familiar with, acquainted with, conversant with". Note that "conversant with" conveys a similar sense to "well versed in", but the preposition cannot be transferred.

 

• Option 4: "on" is used with "an authority on, an expert on a subject", as in *He is an authority on ancient coins.*

 

NOTE

 

• Adjective-preposition pairs frequently tested in SSC: absorbed in, deficient in, interested in, involved in, proficient in, angry with, popular with, jealous of, capable of, devoid of, aware of, eligible for, famous for and grateful to.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A brief appearance by a well-known person in a film or play.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cameo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "cameo" is a brief appearance by a distinguished or well-known person in a film, play or television programme, usually in a small but noticeable role. (संक्षिप्त भूमिका)
◦ Example: The veteran actor made a cameo appearance in the film's closing scene.

 

• The word originally referred to a small piece of jewellery carved in relief, and came to mean any small, finely finished piece of work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Sequel (अगली कड़ी): A film, book or play that continues the story of an earlier one.

 

• Option 3: Prequel (पूर्वकथा): A work whose story takes place before that of an existing work.

 

• Option 4: Montage (दृश्य-संयोजन): A sequence made by combining several short shots or images into one continuous piece.

 

NOTE

 

• Other cinema and media terms often tested: Teaser (a very short promotional clip), Trailer (a longer preview), Spoiler (a revelation of crucial plot details), Cast (the actors in a production), Cameo and Blockbuster (an extremely successful film).

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A word or phrase that reads the same both forwards and backwards.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Palindrome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "palindrome" is a word, phrase or number that reads the same from left to right as from right to left. (विलोमपद)
◦ Examples: *level, madam, refer, rotator, civic, noon, malayalam*; and the sentence *"Madam, I'm Adam."*

 

• The word comes from the Greek *palin* (again) and *dromos* (running) — literally "running back again".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Acronym (संक्षिप्ताक्षर): A word formed from the initial letters of other words and pronounced as a word — *NASA, RADAR, LASER, SCUBA*. When the letters are pronounced separately, as in *UPSC* or *SSC*, it is called an initialism.

 

• Option 3: Pseudonym (उपनाम / छद्म नाम): A fictitious name adopted by an author — *Mark Twain* for Samuel Clemens.

 

• Option 4: Antonym (विलोम शब्द): A word opposite in meaning to another.

 

NOTE

 

• Related terms frequently asked: Anagram (a word formed by rearranging the letters of another, as *listen → silent*), Homonym (same spelling or sound, different meaning), Homophone (same sound, different spelling), Synonym (same meaning) and Eponym (a name from which something takes its title).

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Do the students submit their assignments online?
option_1: Are the assignments submitted online by the students?
option_2: Is the assignments submitted online by the students?
option_3: Were the assignments submitted online by the students?
option_4: Have the assignments been submitted online by the students?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Are the assignments submitted online by the students?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Present Tense beginning with the auxiliary "Do".

 

• Rule — Simple Present, interrogative:
◦ Active: Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object?
◦ Passive: Is/Am/Are + Object + V3 + by + Subject?

 

• Applying the rule: the object "their assignments" becomes the subject "the assignments"; it is plural, so the auxiliary is "Are"; "submit" becomes the past participle "submitted"; and "the students" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: *Are the assignments submitted online by the students?*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 is incorrect — "Is" is singular, whereas the new subject "the assignments" is plural. This is a subject-verb agreement error.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect — "Were submitted" is the passive of the Simple Past Tense.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect — "Have been submitted" is the passive of the Present Perfect Tense.

 

NOTE

 

• The possessive adjective "their" is replaced by "the" when the object becomes the subject of the passive sentence.

 

• In interrogative sentences the auxiliary always comes first, before the new subject.

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

The carpenter was repairing the broken chair.
option_1: The broken chair was repaired by the carpenter.
option_2: The broken chair had been repaired by the carpenter.
option_3: The broken chair is being repaired by the carpenter.
option_4: The broken chair was being repaired by the carpenter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The broken chair was being repaired by the carpenter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is an assertive sentence in the Past Continuous Tense (was/were + V-ing).

 

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject

 

• Applying the rule: the object "the broken chair" becomes the subject; it is singular, so the auxiliary is "was"; "being" must be inserted; "repairing" becomes the past participle "repaired"; and "the carpenter" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: *The broken chair was being repaired by the carpenter.*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is incorrect — "was repaired" omits "being" and therefore expresses the Simple Past, not the Past Continuous.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect — "had been repaired" is the passive of the Past Perfect Tense.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect — "is being repaired" is the passive of the Present Continuous Tense.

 

NOTE

 

• Only the continuous tenses insert "being" before the past participle:
◦ Present Continuous — *is/am/are being + V3*
◦ Past Continuous — *was/were being + V3*

 

• The Perfect Continuous and Future Continuous tenses are not normally used in the passive voice.

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice?

Had the prize been awarded by the chief guest?
option_1: Did the chief guest award the prize?
option_2: Has the chief guest awarded the prize?
option_3: Had the chief guest awarded the prize?
option_4: Was the chief guest awarding the prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Had the chief guest awarded the prize?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is an interrogative sentence in the Past Perfect Tense, passive voice (Had + object + been + V3 + by + agent?).

 

• Rule — Past Perfect, interrogative:
◦ Passive: Had + Object + been + V3 + by + Subject?
◦ Active: Had + Subject + V3 + Object?

 

• Applying the rule: the agent "the chief guest" becomes the subject, the auxiliary "Had" is retained so that the tense is preserved, and "been awarded" becomes simply "awarded" (the past participle that follows "had").
◦ Active: *Had the chief guest awarded the prize?*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is incorrect — "Did ... award" is the Simple Past Tense and loses the sense of an action completed before another past event.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect — "Has ... awarded" is the Present Perfect Tense.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect — "Was ... awarding" is the Past Continuous Tense, expressing an ongoing rather than a completed action.

 

NOTE

 

• The tense must be preserved exactly when the voice is changed. Compare the interrogative pairs:
◦ *Has the work been done?* → *Has he done the work?*
◦ *Had the work been done?* → *Had he done the work?*
◦ *Will the work be done?* → *Will he do the work?*

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice?

Where was the treaty signed by the two nations?
option_1: Where did the two nations sign the treaty?
option_2: Where do the two nations sign the treaty?
option_3: Where have the two nations signed the treaty?
option_4: Where had the two nations signed the treaty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Where did the two nations sign the treaty?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is a wh-type interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense, passive voice (Wh-word + was/were + object + V3 + by + agent?).

 

• Rule — Simple Past, wh-interrogative:
◦ Passive: Wh-word + was/were + Object + V3 + by + Subject?
◦ Active: Wh-word + did + Subject + V1 + Object?

 

• Applying the rule: the question word "Where" stays at the beginning; the agent "the two nations" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "did" is introduced for the Simple Past interrogative; and "signed" reverts to the base form "sign", because only V1 can follow "did".
◦ Active: *Where did the two nations sign the treaty?*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 is incorrect — "do ... sign" is the Simple Present Tense.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect — "have ... signed" is the Present Perfect Tense.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect — "had ... signed" is the Past Perfect Tense.

 

NOTE

 

• A frequent trap: after "did", the verb must always be in its base form (V1) — *did sign*, never *did signed*.

 

• Remember that the wh-word retains its position at the head of the sentence in both voices.

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The accused appeared to be completely devoid ______ any sense of remorse.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective "devoid" is always followed by the preposition "of", meaning entirely lacking in or free from something. (सर्वथा रहित)
◦ Example: His speech was devoid of any substance.

 

• The completed sentence reads: *The accused appeared to be completely devoid of any sense of remorse.*

 

• "Devoid" is used only in this construction — it cannot stand before a noun, so one says *a man devoid of fear*, never *a devoid man*.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "from" is used with "free from, different from, prevent from, refrain from, abstain from".

 

• Option 2: "in" is used with "deficient in, lacking in, absorbed in". Note that "lacking in" takes "in" while "devoid of" takes "of" — a distinction often tested.

 

• Option 4: "with" is used with "filled with, endowed with, fraught with, conversant with".

 

NOTE

 

• Adjectives that regularly take "of": devoid of, capable of, aware of, desirous of, guilty of, envious of, fond of, proud of, confident of, ignorant of, suspicious of and void of.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The letter had been lying unopened on the corner table for three whole days.

A. Her hands trembled a little as she finally broke the seal.

B. She had recognised the handwriting the moment the postman placed it in her palm.

C. Inside were only four lines, written in a hurried, uneven scrawl.

D. Every morning she had walked past it, and every evening she had told herself that tomorrow would do.

S2. She read them twice, folded the paper carefully, and smiled for the first time in months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BDAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – B – D – A – C – S2, which moves from recognition → avoidance → opening → contents.

 

• S1 → B: S1 tells us the letter lay unopened for three days. B explains the background — she had recognised the handwriting the moment she received it. This recognition is what makes the delay meaningful, so B naturally follows.

 

• B → D: D describes the three days of avoidance — *"Every morning she had walked past it, and every evening she had told herself that tomorrow would do."* This expands on the "three whole days" of S1 and must come before the letter is opened.

 

• D → A: A contains the decisive word "finally", which marks the end of the period of delay described in D. She breaks the seal.

 

• A → C: C describes what was "Inside" — the four hurried lines. The contents can be described only after the seal has been broken.

 

• C → S2: S2 says she read "them" twice, the pronoun referring to the four lines in C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (DBAC) is incorrect because the recognition of the handwriting (B) happened at the moment of delivery and must precede the days of walking past it (D).

 

• Option 3 (BADC) is incorrect because it places the opening of the letter (A) before the period of hesitation (D), and leaves D stranded after the seal is broken.

 

• Option 4 (DBCA) is incorrect because the contents (C) cannot be described before the letter is opened (A).

 

NOTE

 

• Useful clues here: the adverb "finally" marks the end of a delay; the word "Inside" presupposes an opening; and the pronoun "them" in S2 must have the four lines of C as its antecedent.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The stranger who sat opposite me in the railway compartment did not speak for the first two hours.

A. He asked whether I too was travelling to the same town, and I said that I was.

B. Somewhere past midnight he suddenly closed it and turned towards me.

C. He kept a small, worn notebook open on his lap and wrote in it steadily.

D. From that moment until dawn he did not stop talking.

S2. When the train drew in, he shook my hand warmly and disappeared into the crowd without telling me his name.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. CBAD.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct sequence is S1 – C – B – A – D – S2, moving from silence → the break in silence → the first words → the flood of talk.

 

• S1 → C: S1 states that the stranger did not speak for two hours. C tells us what he was doing during that silence — writing steadily in a worn notebook. It fills in the very period S1 describes.

 

• C → B: B begins with the time marker "Somewhere past midnight" and refers to "it", the notebook introduced in C. He closes it and turns towards the narrator, breaking the silence.

 

• B → A: A gives his first words — the question about the destination. This must follow the moment he turns towards the narrator.

 

• A → D: D opens with "From that moment", pointing back to the beginning of the conversation in A, and describes how he talked until dawn.

 

• D → S2: S2 concludes with the arrival of the train and his departure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (BCAD) is incorrect because B contains the pronoun "it", which has no antecedent unless the notebook of C has already been mentioned.

 

• Option 2 (BCDA) is incorrect on both counts — it opens with an unanchored pronoun and places the continuous talking (D) before the conversation has begun (A).

 

• Option 3 (CABD) is incorrect because he could not have spoken (A) before closing the notebook and turning towards the narrator (B).

 

NOTE

 

• The decisive clue in this question is the pronoun "it" in sentence B. In para-jumbles, a sentence containing an unexplained pronoun can almost never come first in the jumbled portion.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question based on the passage.

 

The invention of movable type in Europe in the middle of the fifteenth century is often described as a technological event, but its deeper significance was social. Before printing, a book was copied by hand, and each copy differed slightly from the one before it. Errors multiplied silently across generations of manuscripts, and no two readers could be certain that they were arguing about the same text. Printing did not merely make books cheaper and more numerous; it made them identical. For the first time a scholar in Paris and a scholar in Krakow could refer to the same page of the same edition and know that they were looking at the same words.
This standardisation had consequences that the early printers themselves could not have foreseen. Because errors were now fixed rather than fluid, they could be identified, catalogued and corrected in later editions, so that knowledge began to accumulate instead of merely circulating. Because editions could be dated, scholars could trace how an argument had developed over time. And because a printed attack could be answered by a printed reply within months, disagreement itself became public and continuous rather than private and occasional.
It is therefore misleading to say simply that printing spread ideas. It would be nearer the truth to say that printing changed the conditions under which ideas could be tested.

 

According to the passage, what was the most significant consequence of printing for books?
option_1: It made books far cheaper than handwritten manuscripts.
option_2: It reduced the number of scribes employed in monasteries.
option_3: It made every copy of a given edition identical.
option_4: It replaced Latin with the vernacular languages of Europe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. It made every copy of a given edition identical.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage states the point explicitly: *"Printing did not merely make books cheaper and more numerous; it made them identical."*

 

• The construction "did not merely ... ; it ..." is the author's way of setting aside the obvious effect (cheapness and quantity) in order to emphasise the one he considers truly significant — standardisation.

 

• The next sentence confirms it: a scholar in Paris and one in Krakow could now refer to the same page of the same edition "and know that they were looking at the same words."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is mentioned in the passage, but only as the effect the author explicitly sets aside as *not* the deeper significance. A detail that the passage deliberately subordinates cannot be the "most significant" consequence.

 

• Option 2 is not stated anywhere; the passage refers to copying by hand only to describe the situation before printing.

 

• Option 4 goes beyond the passage altogether — the question of language is never raised.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch for concessive structures such as *"not merely X but Y"*, *"it is not so much X as Y"* and *"less X than Y"*. In each case the emphasis falls on the second element, and that is where the answer usually lies.

Why does the author describe the multiplication of errors in manuscripts as taking place "silently"?

• Option 3 takes the word "silently" literally and applies it to the manner of reading, which is not the author's point at all.

 

NOTE

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the nationalisation of banks in India?

I. Fourteen major commercial banks were nationalised in 1969.

II. Six more commercial banks were nationalised in 1980.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. (बैंक राष्ट्रीयकरण — 1969 में 14 बैंक, 1980 में 6 बैंक)

 

• Statement I is correct: on 19 July 1969, the Government of India under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 major commercial banks, each having deposits of ₹50 crore or more. It was carried out first through an ordinance and then by the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970.

 

• Statement II is correct: a second round of nationalisation took place on 15 April 1980, when 6 more banks with deposits of ₹200 crore or more were nationalised, taking the total to 20. New Bank of India was later merged with Punjab National Bank in 1993, reducing the number to 19.

 

• The stated objectives were to widen branch expansion in rural areas, extend credit to priority sectors such as agriculture and small industry, mobilise savings and end the control of banking by a few business houses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Imperial Bank of India was converted into the State Bank of India in 1955 on the recommendation of the Gorwala Committee — this was in effect the first major nationalisation in Indian banking.

 

• The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

 

• Other landmark nationalisations: life insurance in 1956 (LIC), general insurance in 1972 (GIC) and coal mines in 1973.

 

• In 2017 the five Associate Banks and the Bharatiya Mahila Bank were merged with SBI, and a large-scale amalgamation of public sector banks took effect on 1 April 2020, reducing their number to 12.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect, because both the given statements are factually accurate.

question: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brihadratha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. He was assassinated in about 185 BCE by his own commander-in-chief, Pushyamitra Shunga, who then founded the Shunga dynasty with its capital at Pataliputra. (बृहद्रथ — अंतिम मौर्य शासक)

 

• The event is recorded by Bana in his "Harshacharita", which states that Pushyamitra killed his master while reviewing the army.

 

• The Mauryan line of rulers: Chandragupta Maurya (321-297 BCE) → Bindusara (297-273 BCE) → Ashoka (268-232 BCE), followed by weaker successors such as Dasharatha, Samprati, Shalishuka, Devavarman, Shatadhanvan and finally Brihadratha.

 

• The Mauryan Empire was founded in 321 BCE by Chandragupta Maurya with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), after overthrowing Dhana Nanda, the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Causes usually given for the decline of the Mauryan Empire: highly centralised administration dependent on a strong ruler, weak successors after Ashoka, financial strain, the partition of the empire, and pressure from the north-west.

 

• Important sources for Mauryan history: Kautilya's Arthashastra, Megasthenes's Indica, the Ashokan edicts, Vishakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa and the Buddhist texts Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa.

 

• Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

 

NOTE

 

• Dasharatha (Option 1): A grandson of Ashoka who ruled the eastern part of the empire and granted the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas.

 

• Samprati (Option 2): Another grandson of Ashoka, remembered in Jain tradition as a great patron of Jainism.

 

• Shalishuka (Option 4): A later Mauryan ruler mentioned in the Gargi Samhita, but not the last.

question: The loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is transpiration.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, chiefly through the stomata present on the leaves. (वाष्पोत्सर्जन)

 

• Roughly 90 to 95 per cent of transpiration takes place through the stomata; smaller amounts occur through the cuticle (cuticular transpiration) and through lenticels (lenticular transpiration).

 

• Its importance:
◦ It creates the transpiration pull, the principal force that draws water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots through the xylem.
◦ It cools the plant, much as sweating cools the human body.
◦ It helps in the absorption and distribution of minerals.

 

• Because so much water is lost, transpiration is sometimes called a "necessary evil", an expression coined by the plant physiologist J.A. Curtis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Stomata are minute pores bounded by two kidney-shaped guard cells, which open and close them. When the guard cells absorb water and become turgid, the stoma opens; when they lose water and become flaccid, it closes. In desert plants the stomata are often sunken and open at night to reduce water loss.

 

• Water and minerals are conducted upward by the xylem, and prepared food is conducted in both directions by the phloem — a process called translocation.

 

NOTE

 

• Respiration (Option 1): The oxidation of food to release energy; it involves the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide, not the loss of water vapour.

 

• Translocation (Option 2): The transport of food prepared in the leaves to other parts of the plant through the phloem.

 

• Guttation (Option 4): The loss of water in the form of liquid droplets from the margins of leaves through structures called hydathodes, usually at night — not as vapour.

question: Which of the four Vedas deals mainly with music and melodies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samaveda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Samaveda is the Veda of melodies and chants, and is regarded as the root of Indian classical music. (सामवेद — संगीत का मूल)

 

• Its verses are largely drawn from the Rigveda, but they are set to musical notes for singing by the Udgatri priest during sacrifices. It contains 1,549 verses, of which only about 75 are original.

 

• The four Vedas and their character:
◦ Rigveda — the oldest Veda; a collection of 1,028 hymns in 10 mandalas, recited by the Hotri priest. The Gayatri Mantra, addressed to Savitri, occurs in Mandala III, and the Purusha Sukta, describing the origin of the four varnas, in Mandala X.
◦ Yajurveda — deals with the rituals and procedures of sacrifice; recited by the Adhvaryu priest. It has two parts, the Shukla (White) and Krishna (Black) Yajurveda, and is partly in prose.
◦ Samaveda — deals with music; sung by the Udgatri priest.
◦ Atharvaveda — the latest Veda; contains charms, spells and remedies for ailments, and is associated with the Brahma priest. It gives valuable information about the beliefs and practices of ordinary people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vedas are called "Shruti" (that which is heard) and are apaurusheya, that is, not of human authorship. Each Veda has four parts — Samhita, Brahmana, Aranyaka and Upanishad.

 

• The Upanishads are also called Vedanta, meaning the end of the Vedas, and deal with philosophy and metaphysics. The motto "Satyameva Jayate", inscribed on the State Emblem of India, is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

 

• The six Vedangas are Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhanda and Jyotisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Rigveda (Option 1): The oldest, containing hymns of praise; the source of most Samavedic verses but not itself the Veda of music.

 

• Yajurveda (Option 3): The Veda of sacrificial formulae and procedure.

 

• Atharvaveda (Option 4): The Veda of magical charms, medicine and popular belief.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Secretariat of Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 98.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 98 of the Constitution provides for the Secretariat of Parliament. (संसद का सचिवालय — अनुच्छेद 98)

 

• It lays down that each House of Parliament shall have a separate secretarial staff, though provision may be made by law for the creation of posts common to both Houses. Parliament may by law regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to the secretarial staff, and until then the President may make rules after consulting the Speaker or the Chairman.

 

• The corresponding provision for the States is Article 187, which deals with the Secretariat of the State Legislature.

 

• Both Articles fall in Part V (the Union) and Part VI (the States) of the Constitution respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Articles relating to Parliament:
◦ Article 79 — Constitution of Parliament (President, Council of States, House of the People)
◦ Article 80 — Composition of the Rajya Sabha
◦ Article 81 — Composition of the Lok Sabha
◦ Article 83 — Duration of the Houses
◦ Article 93 — The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People
◦ Article 100 — Voting in the Houses and the quorum
◦ Article 105 — Powers and privileges of the Houses and their members
◦ Article 108 — Joint sitting of both Houses
◦ Article 110 — Definition of a Money Bill
◦ Article 112 — Annual Financial Statement (the Budget)
◦ Article 123 — Ordinance-making power of the President

 

NOTE

 

• Article 93 (Option 1): Provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

 

• Article 105 (Option 3): Deals with the powers, privileges and immunities of Parliament and its members.

 

• Article 118 (Option 4): Empowers each House to make rules of procedure for the conduct of its business.

question: The direct change of a substance from the solid state to the gaseous state without passing through the liquid state is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sublimation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sublimation is the process in which a substance changes directly from the solid state to the gaseous state on heating, without passing through the intermediate liquid state. The reverse process, gas to solid directly, is called deposition. (ऊर्ध्वपातन)

 

• Substances that sublime include camphor, naphthalene (moth balls), ammonium chloride, iodine, dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) and anthracene.

 

• Sublimation is used to separate a sublimable solid from a non-sublimable impurity — for example, camphor mixed with sand.

 

• The other changes of state:
◦ Melting (fusion) — solid to liquid
◦ Freezing (solidification) — liquid to solid
◦ Vaporisation (boiling/evaporation) — liquid to gas
◦ Condensation — gas to liquid

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three states of matter differ in the arrangement of their particles. Solids have a fixed shape and fixed volume; liquids have no fixed shape but a fixed volume; gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume. The fourth state is plasma, found in the sun and stars and in fluorescent tubes, and the fifth is the Bose-Einstein Condensate, predicted by Satyendra Nath Bose and Albert Einstein.

 

• Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released during a change of state at constant temperature. The latent heat of fusion of ice is 3.34 × 10⁵ J/kg, and the latent heat of vaporisation of water is 22.5 × 10⁵ J/kg.

 

NOTE

 

• Condensation (Option 2): The change from the gaseous to the liquid state, as when steam turns into water on a cold surface.

 

• Evaporation (Option 3): The change from liquid to gas at the surface, occurring at all temperatures below the boiling point. It is a cooling process.

 

• Fusion (Option 4): Another word for melting, the change from solid to liquid.

question: The traditional folk songs known as 'Sohar', popular in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, are sung on which occasion?
option_1: The sowing of the first crop
option_4: The departure of a bride to her new home
solution_text:
The correct answer is The birth of a child.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sohar is a traditional folk song of northern India, sung to celebrate the birth of a child, and is especially popular in the Bhojpuri, Awadhi and Magadhi speaking regions of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. (सोहर — शिशु जन्म के अवसर पर गाया जाने वाला लोकगीत)

 

• The songs are sung by women in groups, usually to the accompaniment of the dholak and clapping. Their themes are joy at the arrival of the newborn, blessings for the child's long life and prosperity, and often episodes from the birth of Rama or Krishna.

 

• Sohar belongs to the category of sanskar geet, or life-cycle songs, which mark the important stages of life — birth, the sacred thread ceremony, marriage and so on.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk songs of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar:
◦ Kajari — sung in the month of Sawan during the rainy season
◦ Chaiti — sung in the month of Chaitra
◦ Birha — the songs of separation, associated with the Ahir community
◦ Barahmasa — songs describing the twelve months
◦ Alha — heroic ballads of the warriors Alha and Udal
◦ Vidaai / Banna-Banni — marriage songs, sung at the bride's farewell

 

• Folk songs of other regions frequently asked: Mand (Rajasthan), Baul (West Bengal), Powada (Maharashtra), Ovi (Maharashtra and Goa), Wanawan (Jammu & Kashmir) and Pandavani (Chhattisgarh).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 describes sowing and harvest songs such as Kajari and the various fasal geet.

 

• Option 2 describes monsoon songs, of which Kajari is the best known.

 

• Option 4 describes the Vidaai songs sung when a bride leaves for her husband's home — a different category of sanskar geet altogether.

question: As per the National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5, 2019-21), the sex ratio of the total population in India was ______ females per 1,000 males.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1,020.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5), conducted in 2019-21, the sex ratio of the total population was 1,020 females per 1,000 males. (एनएफएचएस-5 — लिंगानुपात 1,020)

 

• This was the first time in any NFHS survey, and indeed since the first synchronous census of 1881, that women were recorded as outnumbering men in the survey population. In NFHS-4 (2015-16) the figure had been 991.

 

• Within NFHS-5, the sex ratio was 1,037 in rural areas and 985 in urban areas.

 

• The sex ratio at birth for children born in the five years preceding the survey was 929 female births per 1,000 male births, which shows that the imbalance at birth still persists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NFHS-5 was conducted by the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, the nodal agency, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It covered 707 districts across 28 States and 8 Union Territories.

 

• Other key NFHS-5 findings: the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) fell to 2.0, below the replacement level of 2.1; institutional births rose to 88.6%; and 99.6% of households in urban areas and 95.7% overall had access to electricity.

 

• By comparison, Census 2011 recorded a sex ratio of 943, and the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of 919. Kerala has the highest sex ratio among the States and Haryana the lowest.

 

NOTE

 

• 972 (Option 1): Does not correspond to any NFHS figure for the overall sex ratio.

 

• 991 (Option 2): The sex ratio recorded in NFHS-4 (2015-16), the previous round of the survey.

 

• 1,045 (Option 4): Higher than any figure reported by the NFHS.

question: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Chelmsford.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921, and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place during his tenure, on 13 April 1919. (जलियाँवाला बाग हत्याकांड — लॉर्ड चेम्सफोर्ड)

 

• The massacre occurred at Amritsar, where a peaceful gathering assembled on Baisakhi day to protest against the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of leaders Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal. General Reginald Dyer ordered his troops to fire without warning on the enclosed crowd. Michael O'Dwyer was then the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest, and Sir Shankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council. The Hunter Commission was appointed to inquire into the incident. Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940.

 

• Other important events of Chelmsford's tenure: the Lucknow Pact (1916), the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), the Montagu Declaration (1917), the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms / Government of India Act 1919, the Rowlatt Act (1919) and the beginning of the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced dyarchy in the provinces, dividing subjects into transferred and reserved, and provided for a bicameral legislature at the centre.

 

• Viceroys and their landmark associations: Lord Curzon — Partition of Bengal (1905); Lord Minto — Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) and separate electorates; Lord Hardinge — transfer of the capital to Delhi (1911); Lord Reading — Chauri Chaura and the Moplah rebellion; Lord Irwin — Simon Commission and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; Lord Mountbatten — the last Viceroy and first Governor-General of independent India.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Curzon (Option 1): Viceroy from 1899 to 1905; associated with the Partition of Bengal.

 

• Lord Reading (Option 3): Viceroy from 1921 to 1926, immediately after Chelmsford.

 

• Lord Minto (Option 4): Viceroy from 1905 to 1910; associated with the Indian Councils Act of 1909.

question: The Dandi March led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 covered a distance of approximately ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 385 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dandi March, also called the Salt Satyagraha, covered a distance of about 385 km (240 miles) from the Sabarmati Ashram at Ahmedabad to Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat. (दांडी मार्च — लगभग 385 किमी)

 

• It began on 12 March 1930 with 78 chosen volunteers and concluded on 6 April 1930, when Gandhi broke the salt law by picking up a lump of natural salt from the seashore. The march took 24 days.

 

• The breaking of the salt law marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Salt was chosen deliberately because the tax on it affected the poorest households and made the injustice of colonial rule immediately intelligible to everyone.

 

• Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana Satyagraha in May 1930, and C. Rajagopalachari led a parallel salt march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Civil Disobedience Movement was suspended after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 5 March 1931, under which Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference in London, which he attended as the sole Congress representative.

 

• The movement had been preceded by the Lahore Session of the Congress (December 1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, which adopted the resolution of Purna Swaraj; 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

 

• Other major movements led by Gandhi: Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918), Kheda (1918), Non-Cooperation (1920-22) and Quit India (1942).

 

NOTE

 

• 241 km (Option 1) is the figure often confused with the march's length in miles (240 miles), but the distance in kilometres is about 385.

 

• 450 km (Option 3) and 520 km (Option 4) are considerably greater than the actual distance covered.

question: How many languages are currently included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution currently contains 22 languages. (आठवीं अनुसूची — 22 भाषाएँ)

 

• At the commencement of the Constitution in 1950 it contained 14 languages. The additions since then have been:
◦ Sindhi — added by the 21st Amendment, 1967
◦ Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali — added by the 71st Amendment, 1992
◦ Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali — added by the 92nd Amendment, 2003

 

• Sanskrit has the fewest speakers among the scheduled languages, and Hindi the most.

 

• The Eighth Schedule is referred to in Articles 344(1) and 351 of the Constitution. Its purpose is to enable representation on the Official Language Commission and to enrich Hindi, and the languages are also used for examinations conducted by the UPSC and SSC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 343 declares Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union. India has no national language.

 

• Languages that have been granted the status of a classical language include Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014) and, in 2024, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali.

 

• Census 2011 recorded 121 languages and 270 mother tongues with more than 10,000 speakers, out of 1,369 rationalised mother tongues.

 

NOTE

 

• 18 (Option 1) was the number of scheduled languages between 1992 and 2003, after the addition of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali.

 

• 24 (Option 3) and 26 (Option 4) are incorrect. Several languages, including Bhojpuri, Rajasthani, Tulu and Garhwali, have long been under demand for inclusion, but none has yet been added.

question: India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication plant, being set up by Tata Electronics in partnership with Powerchip (PSMC) of Taiwan, is located at Dholera in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication plant (fab) is being established at Dholera in Gujarat by Tata Electronics in partnership with Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) of Taiwan, under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). (धोलेरा, गुजरात — भारत का पहला वाणिज्यिक सेमीकंडक्टर फैब)

 

• The project involves an investment of about ₹91,000 crore and is designed for a capacity of up to 50,000 wafers per month. It will produce chips for the automotive, computing, communication and artificial-intelligence markets.

 

• Other approved semiconductor projects: the Micron assembly, testing and packaging (ATMP) unit at Sanand, Gujarat; a CG Power-Renesas unit at Sanand; a Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test facility at Jagiroad, Assam; and a Kaynes Semicon unit at Sanand.

 

• The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in 2021 under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore, to build a sustainable semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystem in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dholera is being developed as a greenfield Special Investment Region (SIR) and is a node of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC).

 

• A semiconductor is a material whose electrical conductivity lies between that of a conductor and an insulator; silicon and germanium are the commonest examples. Adding impurities to change conductivity is called doping.

 

• Semiconductors are often described as the "new oil" because of their strategic importance to modern electronics, defence and automotive industries.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): A major centre for semiconductor design and research, particularly in Bengaluru, but not the location of the first fab.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): A leading electronics manufacturing state, but the first fab is not located there.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Has emerging electronics investments, but no fabrication plant of this kind.

question: A sound wave has a frequency of 4 kHz and a wavelength of 40 cm. How long (in seconds) will it take to travel a distance of 8 km?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Given: frequency f = 4 kHz = 4,000 Hz; wavelength λ = 40 cm = 0.4 m; distance d = 8 km = 8,000 m.

 

• Step 1 — Find the speed of the wave. The wave equation is:
◦ v = f × λ
◦ v = 4,000 × 0.4 = 1,600 m/s

 

• Step 2 — Find the time taken.
◦ t = distance ÷ speed
◦ t = 8,000 ÷ 1,600 = 5 seconds

 

• Note the unit conversions carefully, since this is where most errors occur: 1 kHz = 1,000 Hz, 1 cm = 0.01 m and 1 km = 1,000 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The wave equation v = fλ applies to all waves, including sound, light and water waves.

 

• Frequency (f) is the number of oscillations per second, measured in hertz (Hz), and is determined by the source. Time period T = 1/f. Wavelength (λ) is the distance between two consecutive compressions or two consecutive rarefactions.

 

• The speed of sound depends on the medium, not on the frequency: about 344 m/s in air at 22°C, 1,500 m/s in water and 5,960 m/s in steel. It increases with temperature, rising by roughly 0.6 m/s for every 1°C rise.

 

• Loudness depends on amplitude, and pitch depends on frequency. Quality (timbre) is what distinguishes two sounds of the same pitch and loudness.

 

NOTE

 

• 3 seconds (Option 1) would result from taking the speed as about 2,667 m/s.

 

• 4 seconds (Option 2) would result from taking the speed as 2,000 m/s — a common error when the wavelength is wrongly converted.

 

• 6 seconds (Option 4) would result from a speed of about 1,333 m/s.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector in India?

I. The MSME sector is largely labour-intensive.

II. The MSME sector requires a very high capital investment per unit of output.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Statement I is correct. (एमएसएमई क्षेत्र — श्रम प्रधान)

 

• Statement I is correct: the MSME sector is labour-intensive, that is, it employs a large number of workers relative to the capital invested. It is the second largest employer in India after agriculture, providing employment to over 11 crore people, and is especially important for rural and semi-urban employment.

 

• Statement II is incorrect: the MSME sector is characterised by a low capital investment per unit of output, which is precisely why it is described as labour-intensive rather than capital-intensive. High capital intensity is a feature of large-scale industries such as steel, petrochemicals and heavy engineering.

 

• MSMEs contribute roughly 30% of India's GDP and about 45% of its exports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The revised classification of MSMEs, effective from 1 July 2020, uses both investment and turnover and applies the same criteria to manufacturing and service enterprises:
◦ Micro — investment up to ₹1 crore and turnover up to ₹5 crore
◦ Small — investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore
◦ Medium — investment up to ₹50 crore and turnover up to ₹250 crore

 

• Registration of MSMEs is done through the Udyam Registration portal.

 

• Major schemes: PMEGP (Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme), CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises), Champions Portal, ZED Certification, PM Vishwakarma and the RAMP programme supported by the World Bank.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect because Statement I is true and Statement II false.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect because Statement II contradicts the defining character of the sector.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because Statement I is undoubtedly correct.

question: The novel 'Sita: Warrior of Mithila' by Amish Tripathi belongs to which of his series?

question: Under the New Industrial Policy of 1991, the number of industries reserved exclusively for the public sector was reduced from 17 to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New Industrial Policy, announced on 24 July 1991, reduced the number of industries reserved exclusively for the public sector from 17 to 8. (नई औद्योगिक नीति 1991 — 17 से घटाकर 8)

 

• The reservation of 17 industries had been made by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, often called the Economic Constitution of India, which classified industries into three schedules.

 

• The eight industries retained in 1991 included arms and ammunition, atomic energy, coal and lignite, mineral oils, the mining of iron ore, manganese, gold and silver, the mining of copper, lead and zinc, atomic minerals, and railway transport.

 

• The number was later reduced further, and at present only two areas — atomic energy and railway operations — remain reserved for the public sector.

 

• The other major measures of the 1991 policy were the abolition of industrial licensing for all but 18 industries (later reduced to a handful), the removal of the MRTP asset limit, liberalised foreign investment up to 51% in 34 priority industries, and the disinvestment of public sector shareholding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The LPG reforms — Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation — were introduced in 1991 under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh, in response to a severe balance of payments crisis in which foreign exchange reserves had fallen to about two weeks' worth of imports.

 

• Other elements of the 1991 reforms: devaluation of the rupee, a loan from the IMF, the abolition of the Controller of Capital Issues, the establishment of SEBI as a statutory body, and tax reforms recommended by the Chelliah Committee.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 1), 10 (Option 3) and 12 (Option 4) do not correspond to the figure fixed by the 1991 policy. The sequence to remember is 17 (1956) → 8 (1991) → 3 (2001) → 2 (at present).

question: In international Hockey, a match consists of four quarters of how many minutes each?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An international hockey match is played in four quarters of 15 minutes each, making a total playing time of 60 minutes. (हॉकी — 4 क्वार्टर, प्रत्येक 15 मिनट)

 

• The format was changed by the International Hockey Federation (FIH) from two halves of 35 minutes to four quarters of 15 minutes, with a 2-minute break between the first and second quarters and between the third and fourth, and a longer halftime interval of 10 minutes.

 

• Each team fields 11 players, including a goalkeeper. The field measures 91.4 m × 55 m, and goals can be scored from a field goal, a penalty corner or a penalty stroke, the last taken from 6.4 m in front of the goal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIH was founded in 1924 and is headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland. Hockey India is the national governing body.

 

• India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey — the greatest tally of any nation — including six in a row from 1928 to 1956. India won bronze at Tokyo 2020 and again at Paris 2024.

 

• Major Dhyan Chand, called "The Wizard of Hockey", won Olympic gold in 1928, 1932 and 1936. His birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day. His autobiography is "Goal".

 

• Important hockey trophies: the Dhyan Chand Trophy, Rangaswami Cup, Beighton Cup, Aga Khan Cup and the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 minutes (Option 1) does not correspond to any period in a hockey match.

 

• 20 minutes (Option 3) is the length of a period in ice hockey, which has three periods of 20 minutes.

 

• 25 minutes (Option 4) is incorrect. Note that the old format was two halves of 35 minutes, which is no longer used.

question: The 'Gol Gumbaz', known for its enormous dome and whispering gallery, is situated in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gol Gumbaz is situated at Vijayapura (formerly Bijapur) in Karnataka. It is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah, the seventh ruler of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur, and was completed in 1656. (गोल गुम्बज — विजयपुरा, कर्नाटक)

 

• Its dome is among the largest domes in the world, with an external diameter of about 44 metres, and it is built without any supporting pillars.

 

• The gallery that runs round the inside of the dome is famous as the "Whispering Gallery", where even a faint sound is repeated several times over and a whisper can be heard clearly at the opposite end. This is a striking illustration of the multiple reflection of sound.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important monuments of Karnataka: the Hampi group of monuments (Vijayanagara Empire, a UNESCO World Heritage Site), the Pattadakal and Aihole temple complexes of the Chalukyas, the Belur, Halebidu and Somnathpur temples of the Hoysalas, the Gommateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola and Mysore Palace.

 

• Other Deccan Sultanate monuments: the Charminar and Golconda Fort at Hyderabad (Qutb Shahi), and the Ibrahim Rauza at Bijapur, sometimes called the "Taj Mahal of the Deccan" for its elegance.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 2): Home of the Charminar, Golconda Fort and the Qutb Shahi tombs.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for the Ajanta, Ellora and Elephanta caves and the Bibi Ka Maqbara.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Known for the Lepakshi temple and the Amaravati stupa.

question: Which of the following is the first Mughal structure to be built as a garden tomb in India, and is regarded as the forerunner of the Taj Mahal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humayun's Tomb at Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Humayun's Tomb at Delhi is the first garden tomb (charbagh) in the Indian subcontinent and is regarded as the architectural forerunner of the Taj Mahal. (हुमायूँ का मकबरा — भारत का पहला बागनुमा मकबरा)

 

• It was commissioned in 1565 by Hamida Banu Begum, the widow of Humayun, and designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas. It was completed in about 1572.

 

• Its features that were later developed at Agra include the charbagh layout — a garden divided into four quarters by water channels, symbolising the gardens of paradise — the high double dome, the use of red sandstone with white marble inlay, and the placing of the tomb on a large plinth with arched recesses.

 

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993. It was in this tomb that the last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, took refuge and was captured by Major Hodson in 1857.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Taj Mahal at Agra was built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal between 1632 and 1653; its chief architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahauri. It is celebrated for its pietra dura inlay work and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

 

• Itimad-ud-daula's tomb at Agra, built by Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg, was the first Mughal structure built entirely of white marble and the first to make extensive use of pietra dura. It is often called the "Baby Taj".

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar's Tomb at Sikandra (Option 1): Begun by Akbar and completed by Jahangir; built mainly of red sandstone and notable for having no dome.

 

• Bibi Ka Maqbara (Option 3): Built by Prince Azam Shah in memory of his mother Dilras Banu Begum; called the "Taj of the Deccan", and much later than Humayun's tomb.

 

• Jahangir's Tomb at Shahdara (Option 4): Located near Lahore in present-day Pakistan; it has four minarets but no dome.

question: India signed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) in July 2025 with which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Kingdom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India signed the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with the United Kingdom on 24 July 2025 in London. (भारत-यूके सीईटीए — जुलाई 2025)

 

• It was concluded after 14 rounds of negotiations spread over about three years, and is India's most comprehensive trade agreement with a G-7 nation, as well as the United Kingdom's most significant bilateral trade agreement since it left the European Union.

 

• Key features: the United Kingdom is to remove duties on about 99% of Indian tariff lines, covering textiles, leather and footwear, marine products, engineering goods, chemicals and pharmaceuticals; and India is to reduce tariffs on a large share of British goods over time. A separate Double Contribution Convention on social security accompanies the agreement, exempting Indian professionals working temporarily in the UK from paying social security contributions in both countries.

 

• The agreement, together with the social security convention, entered into force on 15 July 2026, after the completion of ratification in both countries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other major recent trade agreements: the India-UAE CEPA (2022), the India-Australia ECTA (2022) and the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (2024) with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.

 

• Types of trade agreements, in ascending order of depth: PTA (Preferential Trade Agreement), FTA (Free Trade Agreement), CECA/CEPA/CETA (Comprehensive Economic Cooperation/Partnership/Trade Agreement), Customs Union, Common Market and Economic Union.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 2): India signed the Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA) with Australia in 2022, not a CETA in 2025.

 

• Japan (Option 3): India signed a CEPA with Japan in 2011.

 

• Canada (Option 4): Negotiations for a trade agreement with Canada have been held, but no such agreement was signed in July 2025.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honour, instituted in 1991-92. It was formerly called the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award and was renamed in 2021. The first recipient was Viswanathan Anand in 1991-92.

 

• Other national sports awards: the Arjuna Award (for outstanding performance over four years, instituted 1961), the Dronacharya Award (for coaches, 1985), the Dhyan Chand Award (for lifetime achievement, 2002) and the Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar for organisations.

 

NOTE
