question: Which country won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, defeating New Zealand by four wickets in the final played at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on 9 March 2025. (आईसीसी चैंपियंस ट्रॉफी 2025 — विजेता भारत)

 

• New Zealand scored 251 for 7, and India reached the target at 254 for 6 with an over to spare, KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja seeing the innings home. Rohit Sharma scored 76 and was named Player of the Match.

 

• With this, India won its third Champions Trophy title — after 2002 (shared with Sri Lanka) and 2013 — becoming the most successful team in the history of the tournament. India also became the first team to win the tournament without losing a single match.

 

• The tournament was hosted by Pakistan, with India's matches played at a neutral venue in Dubai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ICC Champions Trophy was first held in 1998 as the ICC KnockOut Trophy, in Bangladesh, and was won by South Africa. It returned in 2025 after a gap of eight years, the previous edition having been held in 2017 and won by Pakistan.

 

• India's other major ICC titles: the ODI World Cup in 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M.S. Dhoni), and the T20 World Cup in 2007 (M.S. Dhoni) and 2024 (Rohit Sharma).

 

• M.S. Dhoni is the only captain to have won all three major ICC white-ball trophies.

 

NOTE

 

• New Zealand (Option 2): The runner-up in 2025; it had won the tournament jointly with India in 2002.

 

• Australia (Option 3): Won the Champions Trophy in 2006 and 2009; it was defeated by India in the semi-final in 2025.

 

• South Africa (Option 4): Winner of the first edition in 1998.

question: As per the IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2025, India ranks ______ in the world in installed wind power capacity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fourth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the IRENA Renewable Energy Statistics 2025 (with data up to December 2024), India ranks fourth in the world in installed wind power capacity. (आईआरईएनए 2025 — पवन ऊर्जा में भारत चौथे स्थान पर)

 

• In the same report, India ranks third in installed solar power capacity and fourth in total renewable energy installed capacity. The countries ahead of India in wind power are China, the United States and Germany.

 

• India's wind power potential is concentrated along the western and southern coasts. Gujarat has the largest installed wind capacity, followed by Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra. The Muppandal wind farm in Tamil Nadu is among the largest in the country.

 

• India has committed to reaching 500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030, announced as part of the Panchamrit commitments at COP-26, Glasgow (2021).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) was founded in 2009 and is headquartered at Abu Dhabi, UAE. India is a member.

 

• The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) at Chennai is the nodal agency for wind resource assessment, functioning under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).

 

• India's other renewable initiatives: the International Solar Alliance (headquartered at Gurugram), the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for rooftop solar, the PM-KUSUM scheme for solar pumps and the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

 

NOTE

 

• First (Option 1): China holds the first position in wind power capacity by a very wide margin.

 

• Second (Option 2) and Third (Option 3): The United States and Germany occupy the second and third positions respectively. Note carefully that India is third in solar but fourth in wind.

question: Lala Lajpat Rai, popularly known as 'Punjab Kesari', was born in the present-day Indian state of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai was born on 28 January 1865 at Dhudike, in the Moga district of Punjab. He is popularly remembered as "Punjab Kesari", the Lion of Punjab. (लाला लाजपत राय — पंजाब केसरी)

 

• He was one of the trio "Lal-Bal-Pal" — Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal — the foremost leaders of the Extremist (Garam Dal) group in the Indian National Congress.

 

• He led the protest against the Simon Commission at Lahore on 30 October 1928, where he was severely injured in a lathi charge ordered by Superintendent James A. Scott, and died on 17 November 1928. His death was avenged by Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru and Chandrashekhar Azad, who shot J.P. Saunders in December 1928.

 

• He founded the Punjab National Bank (1894), the Lakshmi Insurance Company and the Servants of the People Society (1921), and was associated with the Arya Samaj and the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) schools.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• His writings include "The Story of My Deportation", "Unhappy India", "Young India" and a biography of Shivaji. He was deported to Mandalay in 1907 along with Sardar Ajit Singh for his role in the agitation against the Punjab Colonisation Bill.

 

• He presided over the Calcutta Special Session of the Congress in 1920, which approved the Non-Cooperation Movement.

 

• Birthplaces of other leaders frequently asked: Bal Gangadhar Tilak — Ratnagiri, Maharashtra; Bipin Chandra Pal — Sylhet (now in Bangladesh); Subhas Chandra Bose — Cuttack, Odisha; Sardar Patel — Nadiad, Gujarat; Bhagat Singh — Banga, Lyallpur (now in Pakistan).

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 2): Home of leaders such as Sir Chhotu Ram; Lala Lajpat Rai did much of his legal and political work at Hisar, which is in present-day Haryana, but he was born in Moga district, Punjab.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3) and Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with his birth.
